We proceed to find an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1.** We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2.** We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-\frac{22}{11}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3.** We find the vector ${v}_{3}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{11}{11}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{7}{7}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{a}{c}=\frac{3}{1}=3.
$$
